title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $β$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.
summary: This paper provides a detailed mathematical analysis of the long-time behavior of dynamical correlation functions using finite-temperature Fredholm determinants. By employing the Effective Form Factor method, the authors determine the asymptotic profile and fix the necessary finite normalization constant. The results confirm theoretical predictions from generalized hydrodynamics for systems like hard rods.
main_problem: The paper studies the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants for correlation functions.
main_result: The analysis successfully determines the transition profile using parabolic-cylinder functions and fixes the finite normalization constant, showing consistency with generalized hydrodynamics predictions.
method: The authors employ the Effective Form Factor approach, splitting the Fredholm determinant into factors, and solving associated Riccati equations derived from Wronskian analysis.
model_or_system: The study concerns dynamical correlation functions in quantum many-body systems, modeled via generalized sine-kernel Fredholm determinants, with connections drawn to the hard-rod gas and the Gaussian $\beta$ ensemble.
key_observables: Dynamical Fredholm determinant $D_\nu(x, t)$, effective phase shift, and the transition profile.
important_parameters: Finite temperature, long-time/large-distance limits, and the jump parameter $\Delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the outer asymptotics are sufficient for the leading behavior, and it relies on solving sewing conditions around a quadratic saddle point.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the asymptotic form of the determinant, determining the transition profile via solving sewing conditions, and finally fixing the finite normalization constant by matching results from the high-temperature Gaussian ensemble analysis.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques used to analyze the long-time dynamics of correlation functions are highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems, which is a core area of modern AMO and condensed matter theory.
